title: Operator Kitchen Slate and Rollout Cookbook — Nov 2026 (Draft)
content:
Summary:
This 'Operator Kitchen' doc is a hands-on, hour-by-hour cookbook for the upcoming Nov 2026 micro-release of the serving runtime + routing changes. It blends a compact rollout calendar, a prioritized checklist for operators, ambient telemetry thresholds, and a working draft of the release notes we can push to customers after stabilization. Intended audience: on-call operators, release shepherds, SREs and release engineers doing the day-of work.

High-level goals:
- Deploy runtime v2.14.1 with model-routing fallback enabled (opt-in for canary)
- Validate latency SLOs (p50/p95) across US-EAST and EU-WEST pockets
- Keep unit cost delta < 5% for small-batch workloads
- No customer-facing errors > 0.1% during 24h after deploy

Launch window (compact calendar):
- Nov 17, 2026 09:00 UTC — Preflight window (team prep + dry smoke)
- Nov 17, 2026 11:00 UTC — Canary push (5% traffic, US-EAST)
- Nov 17, 2026 12:30 UTC — Canary validation check-in (1.5 hours after canary)
- Nov 17, 2026 14:00 UTC — Gradual ramp to 30% (regional spread to EU-WEST)
- Nov 17, 2026 16:00 UTC — Broad ramp to 100% (if green)
- Nov 17–19, 2026 — Post-deploy watch (72h sampling + quality checks)

Preflight checklist (must be green before 09:00 UTC):
- [ ] Release artifacts built and checksumed (sha256 in release bucket). PR: serving-runtime/pull/8421
- [ ] Canary config file prepared: routing_fallback: true; batch_target_ms: 20–50; quant_profile: q8_eco
- [ ] Nightly synthetic perf-runbench completed on canary nodes (script: infra/smoketest/runbench.sh)
- [ ] Telemetry hooks wired: token-level cost, per-model latency slices, kv-cache hit rate
- [ ] Ops slack channel created: #ops-launch-nov17 (invite SRE, release-eng, product-hosted-api)
- [ ] Pager rotations mapped and acknowledged for Nov 17–19 (primary/secondary/triage)

Canary recipe (5% traffic):
- Targeted cohorts: internal traffic + opt-in beta orgs (customer list in linked artifact)
- Duration: min 60 minutes, preferred 90–120 minutes for steady-state signals
- Validation checks (automated + manual):
  - Automated smoke: create 1000 short text gen requests, track p50/p95 and error rate
  - Manual spot-checks: run conversational regression suite (prompt set: regress/canary-2026-11)
  - Telemetry gating: p50 change < 10% and p95 change < 15%; error rate < 0.05%

Hourly gate cookbook (what operator does at each hour):
- T+0: confirm build hash, mark canary job as running, announce to #ops-launch-nov17
- T+0.5: check basic health (node readiness, pods stable, GPU mem < 80%)
- T+1: review the perf-runbench + synthetic latency curves; run quick uniqueness sample prompts
- T+1.5: decision call -> continue ramp or pause (use decision matrix below)
- T+3: if still green, expand to 30% and monitor EU-WEST regional slices
- T+5: if green at 30% for 2 hours, prepare broad ramp to 100%

Decision matrix (quick):
- Any customer 5xxs increase by >5x: PAUSE and roll traffic back to previous variant
- p95 latency increase >30% sustained for 15 minutes: PAUSE + investigate (telemetry tags: kernel, batch_size, routing)
- KV-cache hit rate drop >10% and token cost spike >7%: consider rollback or route partial traffic away

Rollback ladder (atomic steps):
1) Short-circuit router to previous model variant for affected region (fastest)
2) Scale down new runtime pool, scale up previous pool (graceful draining)
3) Revert deployment in orchestration system and redeploy last stable artifact
4) Postmortem + runbook updates
Notes: prefer 1 -> 2 for speed; use 3 only if the above fail or for configuration-level problems.

Smoke & espresso tests (validation suite):
- Smoke (automated): 200 summarize calls + 200 embed calls across token lengths; assert error rate < 0.1%
- Espresso (manual spot): high-temperature prompt set to flush degenerate outputs; check quality regression flags
- Quality monitoring: quick eval harness (eval/quality/launch-2026-11) to run every 2 hours during watch window

Telemetry thresholds (ambient alerts):
- Latency p50 baseline: 70ms; p95 baseline: 260ms (US-EAST small-batch reference)
- Alert if p50 > baseline * 1.2 OR p95 > baseline * 1.25 for 10m
- Error-rate alert: >0.5% across any region for 5m
- Cost per 1k tokens: alert if +8% vs baseline sustained for 30m

Post-deploy watch plan (72h):
- Day 0 (first 8 hours): 15m cadence checks for first 2 hours, then 30m cadence for next 6 hours. Daily standup at 18:00 UTC.
- Day 1–3: 2h cadence checks; daily digest to stakeholders with metrics snapshot + anomalies
- Quality regressions: if an eval regression score drops >1.5 stddev vs baseline, open immediate investigation ticket (label: regression-hot)

Release notes (working draft):
Version: serving-runtime v2.14.1 (internal build: b-20261117-8421)
Highlights:
- Introduces model-routing fallback capability (opt-in) to allow graceful degradation to smaller quantized variants when capacity constrained.
- Kernel selection improvements for Llama-derived architectures — expected median latency savings ~6–12% for medium-length inputs.
- Minor bugfixes: KV cache eviction race (PR #8399), improved error messages on OOM.
Known issues:
- Edge-case: very long context (>16k) may see slightly higher memory churn during first request; mitigated by rolling kv-cache warmup. Monitor: kv_warmup_count
- Natively-quantized models may show slight output style drift in low-temperature text-gen; customers can pin pre-upgrade model.
Migration notes for customers:
- No forced behavior changes. Model-routing fallback is disabled by default for hosted API customers; product teams can enable via canary flag.
- Operators: if you manage dedicated pools, review quant_profile settings and batch_target_ms to tune cost/latency tradeoff.

Open action items (owner tags):
- [Evan] finalize release bucket and sign artifacts (by 2026-11-06)
- [Priya] prepare customer comms snippet + support playbook (by 2026-11-15)
- [Lucas] run extended regression eval overnight and drop results into eval/quality/ (by 2026-11-09)
- [Sasha] pre-provision temporary capacity in EU-WEST for canary (by 2026-11-14)

Notes to on-call and shepherd:
- Keep the #ops-launch-nov17 channel alive with short updates; prefer timestamps like [T+1.5] to anchor decisions.
- If pausing ramp, capture a short decision note and immediate snapshot: (build hash, region, p50/p95, error rate, top 3 traces). Save to linked artifacts with prefix: launch-notes/2026-11-17
- Postmortem template: use template 'release-postmortem-compact' and include timeline, telemetry graphs, and remediation actions.

Appendix A — handy commands and links:
- Redeploy last stable: infra/orchestrate/revert.sh --env=prod --tag=stable
- Curl smoke harness: infra/smoketest/smoke.sh --host api.redwood.com --count 1000
- Perf runbench: infra/smoketest/runbench.sh --batch-target 30 --duration 5m
- GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/8421
- Jira: JIRA-RELEASE-2026-11 (release epic)

Quick retrospective bits (notes-to-self):
- Keep the canary window long enough to observe diurnal traffic anomalies in EU-WEST (historically shows 11:00–13:00 UTC spikes).
- Consider pre-warming KV cache with targeted prefix set for high-volume customers to avoid cold-start noise in the first hour.
- Next iteration idea: add a 'healthcheck-weight' knob for partial request sampling to drive faster rollback decisions without full 100% measurement.

-- End of draft --
